item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md exactly as its acceptance criteria state. The package is tasktracker/ (module tasktracker/store.py); tests live in tests/.

TT-104 spec (verbatim from BACKLOG.md):
`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add tests for this ticket in a NEW file tests/test_ticket_tt104.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py; other tickets run in parallel). Functions stay under 60 lines, comments minimal. Make exactly one commit for this ticket on your branch with a clear message, using the repository's existing git identity; add no attribution or tool-generated lines to the commit. Do not push. Do not touch files for other tickets (dates.py, export.py, search.py). Report what you changed and the test output.

model_reasons.implement: State mutation with LIFO history; medium is the configured maximum, and the brief spells out the edge cases.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md exactly as its acceptance criteria state. The package is tasktracker/ (module tasktracker/search.py); tests live in tests/.

TT-103 spec (verbatim from BACKLOG.md):
`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add tests for this ticket in a NEW file tests/test_ticket_tt103.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py; other tickets run in parallel). Functions stay under 60 lines, comments minimal. Do not touch files for other tickets (dates.py, export.py, store.py). Report what you changed and the test output.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md exactly as its acceptance criteria state. The package is tasktracker/ (module tasktracker/export.py); tests live in tests/.

TT-102 spec (verbatim from BACKLOG.md):
`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md exactly as its acceptance criteria state. The package is tasktracker/ (module tasktracker/dates.py); tests live in tests/.

TT-101 spec (verbatim from BACKLOG.md):
`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add tests for this ticket in a NEW file tests/test_ticket_tt101.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py, other tickets touch other modules in parallel). Functions stay under 60 lines, comments minimal. Do not touch files for other tickets (export.py, search.py, store.py). Report what you changed and the test output.

pr.body: Approach: InvalidDate(ValueError) in tasktracker/dates.py. Impossible dates come from date() raising ValueError, wrapped in _calendar_date. Unsupported forms raise InvalidDate instead of ValueError. Offsets that overflow timedelta/date are wrapped in _offset_date. today, tomorrow, +0d, +Nd, case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed matching are unchanged. Files: tasktracker/dates.py, tests/test_ticket_tt101.py (new; tests/test_basic.py untouched). Checks: unittest discover, 10 OK. Review: agt_01M89Z5NEASWP5VM82EWQP7R8J passed 324e25e. Follow-up (non-blocking): the days >= 0 assert in _offset_date is decorative because the regex only matches unsigned digits; can be dropped. Assumption: no non-test callers of parse_due exist in the repo, which the reviewer confirmed by grep.
pr.summary: parse_due no longer clamps impossible dates. now raises InvalidDate. before: 2026-02-30 became 2026-02-28; now: InvalidDate naming the input. Bad forms and out-of-range offsets (-3d, 3d) also raise InvalidDate.
pr.title: TT-101: reject impossible and malformed due dates

agt_01M89Z5NEASWP5VM82EWQP7R8J:1.description: _offset_date's assert `days >= 0` is decorative: OFFSET regex `\+(\d+)d` can only produce non-negative values. Could be dropped without loss of safety. Nit only.

risk.why: Contained behaviour change in one public function: impossible dates that were clamped now raise InvalidDate. InvalidDate subclasses ValueError, so existing except ValueError handlers still work. Reviewer confirmed medium. No non-test callers found.
